content.comment_body: Hello, I am planning to use five [product_name] modules with two analog inputs each, along with one [product_name] module with two analog outputs. My setup will have ten transmitters connected, and I’d like the ability to route any transmitter signal to one of the analog outputs, which goes to a digital display. What is the best way to accomplish this?

You can only use up to eight analog inputs, along with one [product_name] module having two analog outputs. For example, you could use a base module with four analog inputs plus additional analog input modules and an analog output module, or use a base module with two analog inputs expanded by more analog input modules and one analog output module. The system supports flexible expansion up to 24 digital inputs, 16 digital outputs, 8 analog inputs, and 2 analog outputs. See more at [url]

[user_name] is correct. You can connect a maximum of four [product_name] analog input modules. This is only possible with a base module type that does not have integrated analog inputs. Routing some of the eight possible analog inputs to an analog output can be achieved with an analog multiplexer.

Only eight analog inputs are possible? That’s unfortunate as I need ten. I’ll need to look for an alternative solution. Regarding the analog multiplexer suggestion, I have already tried one, but encountered 'incompatible connectors' errors. If I only use eight analog inputs, I have eight pressure transmitters (4-20 mA) and one digital display with analog input. I’d like to select which transmitter’s pressure is shown via digital inputs. Based on the measured pressure, I also plan to control valves and alarms.

You intend to send the analog signal to an external display for visibility. What type of signal does the display require—0-10V or 4-20mA? I’ve attached an example demonstrating both methods. For instance, analog inputs from pressure sensors measuring 0-6 bar could route to one analog output (0-10V), while sensors measuring 0-12 bar could route to another output (4-20mA). Digital inputs allow you to select which sensor value is sent to the output. The recommended process: (1) scale the analog inputs, (2) assign them to an analog multiplexer, (3) use an input to select the desired pressure value, (4) scale for the analog output. The output always needs a value from 0-1000 steps, so if your sensor reads up to 1200 steps, the conversion factor is 1000/1200 = 0.83. Configure analog amplifiers using this gain factor. If sensors have varying ranges, you’ll need more multiplexers and amplifiers to handle the scaling. Also see this FAQ: [document]. For handling more than eight sensors, using an external multiplexer or a higher-capacity CPU might be necessary.
Thank you very much for the example—it’s clear what to do now. Just a quick question: are X1 and X2 simply placeholder connectors for displaying pressure?

Without the placeholder connectors labeled X, you cannot download the program to the CPU. Each function block, such as analog threshold triggers, needs to be connected to an output, which can be Q, M, or X.

If receiving readings every 30 seconds is acceptable, you could use four digital outputs to toggle three additional sensors on one analog input, storing the last value in a database and maintaining the readings.
You realize this discussion began in 2009?

analysis.insight_summary: Users aiming to connect more than eight analog inputs faced built-in hardware limits with the [company_name] [product_name] system. The maximum analog inputs supported is eight. The community explored using external multiplexers and advanced configuration steps such as scaling analog inputs, assigning them to multiplexer logic, and output adjustment. Solutions require additional hardware or workaround logic, indicating some user frustration.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expected the [product_name] system to support more than eight analog inputs with simple selection and display options for any transmitter. Ideally, the process would be straightforward and fully integrated into the hardware rather than requiring external circuits or complex logic.
